title: Kernel auto-selection v2: GPU SKU-aware kernel registry + explicit fallback + denylist plumbing
author: Isabella Rossi
description: Motivation: Kernel auto-selection v2 needs to pick kernels that are *stable and fast* for a given GPU SKU (A100 vs H100 vs L40S, and also vendor-specific naming/MIG variants). In v1/v2 prototyping we saw two classes of issues: (1) the same kernel ID is not universally safe across SKUs/driver combos (e.g., long-context prefill kernels with aggressive shared-mem assumptions), and (2) SKU naming inconsistencies across clouds lead to accidental fallbacks that are hard to explain or reproduce. This PR introduces a GPU-SKU dimension in the kernel registry, an explicit fallback precedence that is deterministic and auditable, and denylist plumbing for known-bad (kernel, SKU, driver/CUDA) combinations. Summary of changes: Add `GpuSkuKey` + normalization layer that maps raw runtime GPU identifiers (NVML name, PCI device id, compute capability, MIG profile, cloud instance hint) into a stable canonical key. Extend `KernelRegistry` lookup from `(model_family, kernel_id)` to `(model_family, kernel_id, gpu_sku_key)` with wildcard support. Implement explicit fallback precedence: (1) exact canonical SKU match, (2) SKU family wildcard (e.g., A100-*), (3) compute capability bucket (e.g., sm80/sm90), (4) generic kernel entry, (5) legacy/default kernel (v1-compatible) with a telemetry marker. Add denylist evaluation before final selection; denylist rules can target exact kernel IDs or kernel groups, match GPU SKU keys (exact or glob), and optionally constrain by driver/CUDA ranges. Denylist results are deterministic and include an explicit reason string used in telemetry and debug dumps. Operationally, denylist config is loaded from runtime config (same path as other selector configs) and supports hot reload (with caching keyed by config version). Non-goals: This PR does not change the scoring logic or seq-length bucketing; it only changes candidate availability and selection/fallback semantics once a candidate set exists. Notes on determinism: All matching is order-stable (sorted candidate list + stable rule ordering). Normalization never consults network/remote metadata; it uses local device properties + optional, already-present instance hint string passed from scheduler, and always produces the same canonical key for the same inputs. Telemetry: emits `kernel_registry_match_tier` (exact|family|sm|generic|legacy), `gpu_sku_key`, `gpu_sku_raw`, `denylist_hit` and `denylist_rule_id` (when applicable). These are gated behind existing sampling controls (separate PR adds full decision event). Risk: Incorrect normalization could over-bucket dissimilar SKUs (bad perf) or under-bucket (unnecessary fallback). Mitigations: unit tests covering known raw name variants, golden mapping fixtures, and a runtime debug flag to print normalization inputs/outputs. Rollout: behind the existing v2 feature gate; registry supports both old and new schema during transition (see `KernelRegistry::from_config_v1_compat`).
commits: kernels/registry: add sku-aware lookup + wildcard matching
kernels/registry: implement explicit fallback precedence + reason strings
kernels/denylist: add denylist config schema + matching engine
runtime/config: support denylist hot reload + versioned cache key
telemetry: add match-tier + sku key fields to selection stats
tests: golden fixtures for SKU normalization + fallback ordering
testing: Unit: `registry_matcher_test` (fallback tiers + wildcard precedence), `kernel_denylist_test` (glob matching + versioned cache invalidation), `gpu_sku_key_test` (canonicalization + MIG parsing). Integration: `runtime_selector_integration_test` extended to assert match-tier telemetry and that denylist forces fallback. Local sanity on A100-80GB (sm80) + H100 SXM (sm90) dev runners: selector chooses expected kernels; forcing denylist shows deterministic fallback. Bench note: no performance benchmarking in this PR; microbench coverage for selector overhead is tracked separately.
rollout_plan: 1) Land behind existing kernel auto-selection v2 gate (default off). 2) Enable for perf-canary scenarios (A100/H100/L40S) once telemetry sampling is confirmed safe. 3) Populate initial denylist from known-issues doc (kernel+SKU combos) and validate match-tier distribution in dashboards. 4) Canary in Hosted us-east with allowlisted models; use denylist to quickly quarantine any unstable combos without rolling back the entire v2 selector.
ci_summary: Buildkite: runtime-linux-x86_64 (pass), runtime-unit-tests (pass), runtime-lint (pass), config-compat (pass), gpu-sim-tests (pass). One transient failure on `runtime-unit-tests` due to runner OOM; rerun passed.
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Asked to make fallback precedence explicit and documented in-code, not implied by map iteration order; requested a stable ordering guarantee for wildcard matching. Isabella Rossi: Updated matcher to sort candidates and evaluate tiers in a fixed sequence; added `KernelMatchTier` enum and a golden test that would fail on order changes. Noah Patel: Concerned about determinism and replayability; asked whether normalization could depend on environment variables or scheduler hints. Isabella: Normalization uses only NVML + device props; instance hint is optional and only used as a *tie-breaker* for cloud naming, with full raw inputs emitted in debug mode; added comment and test coverage for identical inputs => identical key. Omar El-Sayed: Requested telemetry fields for match-tier and denylist hits, and to ensure cardinality is bounded (no raw GPU name in high-volume metrics). Isabella: Added `gpu_sku_key` as the primary dimension; raw name only in sampled debug event and/or logs, not in counters. Sahana Iyer: Requested config migration path so older configs don’t crash; asked for proto evolution guidance. Isabella: Implemented `from_config_v1_compat` and added config-compat CI check. Sofia Ivanova: Asked how MIG variants are handled given shared scheduling pools; suggested bucketing MIG profiles to parent SKU unless kernel requires per-profile specialization. Isabella: Current canonical key includes MIG profile when present, but registry entries can wildcard at the SKU-family tier; added guidance in comments and fixtures. Final: Hiro approved after last changes; Noah + Omar approved with minor nits; merged after green CI.
release_notes: Runtime: kernel registry now supports GPU SKU-aware entries with deterministic fallback tiers (exact SKU -> SKU family -> SM bucket -> generic -> legacy).
Runtime: denylist plumbing added for quarantining kernel/SKU/driver combinations; emits selection stats indicating denylist hits and fallback tier.
